title: Append Field
prompt: A React dynamic form adds another field without mutating state. Write a helper that returns a new array with the new value appended to the existing fields.

explanation.beginner:
Example: appendField(["a"], "b") produces ["a","b"]. Copy the old sequence and place the new value after its last element. The old sequence must remain a usable previous state.

Compare “works with empty arrays”: input [[],"first"] produces ["first"]. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Copy the old sequence and place the new value after its last element. The old sequence must remain a usable previous state.

Tempting mistake: push mutates the old array and returns a length, so returning fields.push(value) violates both parts of the contract.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated. Copying n references costs O(n) time and O(n) additional space.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “works with empty arrays”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
